# pixellab: commands, the stdio protocol and MCP

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs-cli.mjs from the command registry: run `npm run docs:cli` after changing a command. Don't edit by hand. -->

`pixellab` reads and edits the pixel art in a `.pixellab` document and publishes it as the SVGs a site inlines. It has three doors onto one command registry (`crates/pixellab/src/registry.rs`): the command line, `pixellab serve --stdio` for the Mac app, and `pixellab serve --mcp` for agents. Every command takes the same params (a JSON Schema object) and returns the same JSON through each door.

## The command line

```
pixellab <group> <verb> [args] [--flags] [--json] [--document <path.pixellab>]
```

The leading words name the command (`scene place` is `scene.place`; the longest match wins). Positionals fill the command's arguments in order; every param is also a `--kebab-case` flag. Booleans: `--flag`, `--no-flag`. Lists: comma-separated (`--at 14,6,1`) or the flag repeated; a list of pairs (pixels) is `3,4 5,6` or the flag repeated. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 command error (or `check` found problems), 2 usage error. With `--json`, errors are `{"error": {"code", "message", "details?"}}` on stderr.

| global flag | |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | print the command's result as JSON |
| `--document` | the .pixellab document (else $PIXELLAB_DOC, ~/.config/pixellab/config.json, or the document in --site) |
| `--site` | a site checkout holding the document (else $PIXELLAB_SITE, the config file, ~/Projects/jlawcordova.github.io) |
| `--out` | write the PNG of a render command to this file |
| `--dry-run` | an edit command shows what it would write (a diff) and writes nothing |
| `--force` | an edit command writes despite validation problems or a file changed on disk |
| `-h, --help` | help for the command or group |

**Edits are one-shot.** A command that edits a doc loads it, applies the edit, validates the doc with the engine, serializes it with the engine and writes it atomically (temp file and rename), then prints what changed and `wrote <file>`. It refuses, writing nothing, when the doc has validation problems (code `invalid`, the problems in `details`) or the file changed on disk while it ran (code `conflict`); `--force` writes anyway. `--dry-run` prints the unified diff it would write, any problems, and writes nothing. With `--json` the result gains `saved: [{ doc, file, wrote, hash }]` or `dryRun: [{ doc, file, diff, problems, conflict }]`. The `doc.*` commands (undo, redo, save…) only make sense in a session, so they run through `pixellab serve`. Every write is a version in the document's history, by `the CLI` (see `history list`).

**One writer per document.** While Pixel Lab has the document open, its server owns it: an edit command sends itself to the app (the edit shows on its stage, and the app saves it before answering), and a read reads the app's open copy. Without the app, the command writes the files itself. `--dry-run` asks the app to save first, then shows the diff against the files. `document migrate` refuses while the app has the document open.

The document comes from `--document`, else `PIXELLAB_DOC`, else `~/.config/pixellab/config.json` (`{"document": "…"}`), else `--site <checkout>` / `PIXELLAB_SITE` / `{"site": "…"}` (the `*.pixellab` under the site's `src/assets/pixel-art/`, or its legacy `source/` folder), else `~/Projects/jlawcordova.github.io`.

## Libraries and palette files

Two file kinds sit beside the `.pixellab` document, for moving art between documents by copying. Nothing links a document to either afterwards.

- **Categories.** An object can carry a `category`, a list of names from the outermost in (`["Nature", "Trees"]`, typed `Nature/Trees` or `Nature › Trees`). A name is 1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, `&`, `'` and `-`, and `All` and `Others` can't be the outermost (they are the Library's own tabs). `object category` sets or clears it, `object list --category` filters by it, and `check` reports a bad one. A category never changes how an object renders or what `art build` writes.
- **`.pixellib`, an object library.** A folder: `library.json` (`format`, `kind: "library"`, `name`, `exportedFrom` and `colors`, the palette colors its objects used at export, never read as a palette) and `objects/*.json`, the same files a document holds, categories included. It has no scenes and no palette. `library export` writes one from all of a document's objects, one category and below it, or a named list, adding every object they extend; it refuses an existing library unless `--replace`. `library import` copies a library's objects in: a taken name gets the first free suffix (`pine-2`) and every `extends` follows; an object identical to the document's, apart from its category, isn't copied; a library `character` that differs isn't copied, and its figures extend the document's. Differing colors need `--accept-differences`, and a color the document lacks needs `--convert '{"wood-5":"wood-3"}'` to a color of the same tier; `--dry-run` shows the plan. An import never changes the palette, the existing objects or the scenes, and is one version in the history. `library info` reads a library, `library category` sets categories in one in place, and `check --library <path>` validates one.
- **`.pixelpal`, a palette file.** One JSON file: `format`, `kind: "palette"`, and the `world` and `outfit` tiers (and `colorNotes`) as in a document's `palette.json`. `palette export` writes the document's palette. `palette import` adds the colors the document lacks, by name, at the end of their tier; it never removes one. A name with another value needs `--keep` or `--use-theirs`, and an import that would pass a tier's cap (32 world, 16 outfit) adds nothing and says how many colors are over; `--only` narrows it. It is one edit and one version.

An agent that is refused with `differs`, `missing_colors` or `palette_differs` asks the owner (`chat_ask`) before it accepts differences, converts a color or chooses a value.

## The stdio protocol

`pixellab serve --stdio [--document <path> | --site <checkout>]` is the Mac app's server: newline-delimited [JSON-RPC 2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification) on stdin and stdout, one message per line. stdout carries nothing but JSON-RPC; logs go to stderr. Requests are answered one at a time, in order. Batches are not supported. Protocol version: 1 (`session.info` reports it).

The server holds a **session**: docs open as in-memory working copies with undo and redo (at most 200 steps; rapid repeats of the same edit within a second, such as a held arrow key or one paint stroke sent as many `object.paint` calls, merge into one step). Every command reads the working copies, so `scene.render` shows unsaved edits. **Edits save themselves:** a doc is written about a second after its last change (`PIXELLAB_AUTOSAVE_MS` changes the pause), and everything is saved when the server stops. A doc with validation problems is not written until they're fixed (`saveState: problems`); one whose file changed on disk is merged, three ways, then written (`saveState: conflict` and `doc.stale` when that clashes). `doc.flush` saves now; `doc.save` saves and closes the version. Undo works across saves.

**Methods** are the command names (`scene.place`, `doc.undo`, … see the reference), plus:

| method | result |
| --- | --- |
| `session.info` | `{ name: "pixellab", version, protocol, pid, document: { root, name, kind, publishDir, siteRoot }, site, sourceDir, stateDir, saves: "direct", owner: { pid, appPid, socket, … }, openedVersion, docs: [DocStatus] }` (`openedVersion`: the history's newest version when the server opened the document, for Revert To › Last Opened); a server whose document another one owns answers with code `owned` and `{ appPid, pid }` instead, and exits |
| `shutdown` | `{ ok: true }`, then the server stops reading and exits 0. It also exits when stdin closes. |

```json
→ {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"scene.place","params":{"name":"hero-island","object":"pine","at":[14,6,1]}}
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"doc.changed","params":{"doc":"scene:hero-island","dirty":true,"canUndo":true,"canRedo":false}}
← {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"doc":"scene:hero-island","changed":true,"summary":"pine placed at column 14, row 6, level 1","path":"198","item":{"object":"pine","at":{"tile":[14,6,1]}}}}
```

**Results** are the command's JSON. The shapes the app needs most:

- `scene.render` / `object.render`: `{ png, scale, viewBox: [x, y, w, h], frame?, width, height, time | frame, items: [{ path, object, at, id?, pose?, bounds: [x, y, w, h] }] }`. `png` is a base64 PNG with a transparent background at an integer `scale`; `bounds` are in output pixels (scale included), for hit-testing; `path` is the item's dotted path (`"5.2"`). An object render's item has `path: null` and the result has its `anchor`. A scene render's `viewBox` is the box the scene publishes at (its own, or the fit to what it paints: `frame` says `"fixed"` or `"fit"`), or the `view` window asked for; a scene without a `viewBox` has no edge, so the app asks for the window it shows. `scene.show` and `scene.list` give the resolved `viewBox` and `frame` too.
- Edits: `{ doc: "scene:<name>" | "object:<name>", changed, summary, ... }`; scene item edits add `path` (the item's path after the edit) and `item`; paint edits add `pixels` (how many changed).
- `DocStatus` (in `session.info` and `doc.status` without a doc): `{ doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }`. `doc.changed` adds `undoLabel`, `redoLabel` (the Edit menu's words, with whose step it is for anyone but the owner: `"Place pine (Claude)"`), `author` (who made the change), `saveState` (`saved`, `pending`, `problems`, `conflict`) and `problems`; `doc.status` with a doc adds those and `file, exists, stale` (the file changed on disk since the doc was opened or last matched it), `undo: [edit summaries]`, `redo: [...]` and `edits` (the edits since the doc last matched its file).
- `doc.save`: `{ doc, file, wrote, hash, bytes, diff, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }` (`wrote` is false when the file already held exactly this text).
- `doc.undo` / `doc.redo` / `doc.revert`: `{ doc, changed, summary, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }`; `doc.reload` adds `reloaded`, `doc.merge` adds `merged`.
- `history.list`: `{ versions: [{ number, startedAt, endedAt, author, edits, files, open }], total }`, newest first; `history.render` is `scene.render`'s or `object.render`'s shape plus `{ version, doc, kind }`, for the Versions sheet's ghost.

**Errors** are JSON-RPC errors with a stable `data.code`:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"scene.move: item is required","data":{"code":"usage","details":["item is required"]}}}
```

| `error.code` | when | `data.code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| -32700 | a line that isn't JSON (`id` is null) | |
| -32600 | not a JSON-RPC 2.0 request | |
| -32601 | no such method | `not_found` |
| -32602 | bad params | `usage` (with `details`: every problem) |
| -32000 | the command ran and failed | `not_found`, `invalid` (validation problems in `details`), `conflict`, `dirty`, `exists`, `ambiguous`, `is_group`, `at_front`, `paint_blocked`, `color_cap`, `load_error`, … |
| -32603 | a bug | `internal` |

**Notifications** from the server (no `id`):

| method | params | when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `doc.changed` | `{ doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo, undoLabel, redoLabel, author, saveState, problems }` | after each edit, undo, redo, save, revert, merge or reload, whoever made it (the app, or a client through the socket), and when a clean open doc reloads because its file changed. Sent before the request's response. |
| `doc.stale` | `{ doc, file }` | an open doc with a save pending whose file changed on disk and whose merge clashed (the app shows Reload and Keep Mine) |
| `files.changed` | `{ files: ["scenes/hero-island.json", …] }` | sources changed on disk (another editor, git, a save), debounced 150 ms |
| `history.changed` | `{ versions: [the latest, as history.list lists it] }` | the document's version history changed |
| `activity.appended` | `{ entries: [{ time, tool, args, ok, summary }] }` | an MCP server logged tool calls |

An open doc without unsaved changes reloads from disk when its file changes; one with a save pending gets the change merged in (`doc.merge`: a three-way line merge of the file into the working copy, keeping its edits) and saves. When both changed the same lines the merge refuses (`merge_conflict`), the server sends `doc.stale`, and the doc stays unsaved until it's reverted or saved with `force`.

**The owner.** The server takes `owners/<key>.lock` in the state dir for its document with an OS file lock, which the system lets go of when the process ends however it ends, and listens on a Unix socket beside it (or in `$TMPDIR` when that path is too long). The CLI and MCP servers send their commands to it: the same JSON-RPC, after a `client.hello { kind: "mcp" | "cli", name, version, protocol, chat? }` that names the author. Their requests run in the server's loop between the app's own, one at a time. A second `serve --stdio` on an owned document answers `session.info` with code `owned` (and the holder's `appPid`) and exits; Pixel Lab then brings the other copy forward. Only the user's own processes can connect.

## MCP

`pixellab serve --mcp [--document <path> | --site <checkout>]` is an MCP server over stdio (protocol `2025-06-18`, hand-written: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`). Tools are the commands with `.` → `_` (`scene.place` → `scene_place`), each with its params as `inputSchema`. A tool's result is `content: [{ type: "text", text: <the result as JSON> }]` plus `structuredContent` (the result); render tools return the PNG as an `image` content block first, so agents can see the art. A failed command is a result with `isError: true` and `structuredContent: { error: { code, message, details? } }`; an unknown tool is a JSON-RPC error.

**Edits apply.** An agent's edit changes the document as it's made, with the agent as its author in the version history: nothing waits for approval. While Pixel Lab has the document open, the server sends every call to the app (the owner sees the edit on the stage, and the app saves it); without the app, it saves each edit itself when the call is done (the result lists `saved`, and `unsaved` for a doc with problems, which stays in memory until they're fixed). `doc_undo` takes back the agent's own latest step and refuses (`not-yours`) when someone else has edited the doc since; `history_undo` takes back a whole version. `--direct` is accepted and ignored.

**The session follows disk.** Before every `tools/call` in a server of its own, a clean doc whose file changed reloads, so the next edit starts from the file. `doc_reload` reloads a doc only when nothing unsaved is lost (code `dirty` with the edits otherwise); `doc_revert`, which drops edits, is annotated destructive. When the app closes the document mid-call, the call fails with `owner-gone` and isn't retried. Left out of the tools: `art_build` (it publishes the SVGs a site inlines; publishing is for a person); `doc_adopt` (it's how an MCP server hands its unsaved copy to Pixel Lab, not an edit); `document_copy` (saving a copy of the document is for a person); `document_migrate` (migrating the document is for a person, in Pixel Lab or with pixellab document migrate).

### Setup for Claude Code

With the app installed by `scripts/install.sh`, point Claude Code at the program inside it (the Agent window's Connect row shows the same command):

```sh
claude mcp add pixellab -- "$HOME/Applications/Pixel Lab.app/Contents/Helpers/pixellab" serve --mcp
```

Or at a release's `pixellab` (`pixellab-darwin-arm64.tar.gz`, `pixellab-linux-x64.tar.gz`), or this repo's build for development (`cargo build --release`):

```sh
claude mcp add pixellab -- /Users/jlawcordova/Projects/jlawcordova-lab/target/release/pixellab serve --mcp
```

Add `--document <path.pixellab>` (or `--site <checkout>`) after `--mcp` for another document, or set `PIXELLAB_DOC`. See what agents did with `pixellab history list` and `pixellab activity list`.

## The state dir: history, owners and activity

The state dir is `$PIXELLAB_STATE`, else `~/Library/Application Support/Pixel Lab/`. Nothing here is part of the document, so a site that publishes the document never sees it. `<key>` is the first 16 hex digits of the sha256 of the document's real path.

- `history/<key>/`: the document's versions. `versions.jsonl` has one `{ number, startedAt, endedAt, author, edits, changes: [{ file, before, after }], open }` per line, `before` and `after` being the sha256 of the file's text in `blobs/<sha256>.json` (null: no file). Version 0 is the document as first opened. A version is a stretch of one author's writes (`owner`, `agent`, `cli`, `outside`, `restore`), closed when someone else writes, after a minute's pause, by `history.mark` or `doc.save`, or when the document closes. Versions older than a day thin to one a day, older than 30 days to one a week.
- `owners/<key>.lock` and `<key>.sock`: the app's server that owns the document while it's open: `{ pid, appPid, document, socket, protocol, version, startedAt }`, held with an OS file lock.
- `activity.jsonl`: one line per MCP `tools/call`: `{ time, tool, args, ok, summary }` (`tool` is the MCP tool name).
- `retired-proposals/`: proposals left from before edits applied, moved here once with a `notice.json` (`{ count, dir, at }`) that the Agent window shows.

| `--limit` | integer | default `50` | how many entries (1 to 1000) |

### art

#### art.build

Publish: validate every source, compile each scene with an output and write the SVGs.

```
pixellab art build [--dir <text>]
```

Validates the document's files on disk (unsaved working copies aren't in it; unsaved lists them), renders each scene with an `output` to a rect SVG, merges each color group into one <path>, checks the result lossless, and writes <publish dir>/<output>. A scene with an `image` is also rendered on the preview card color to a PNG, written to the manifest's publish.images (else --dir). Over the budget (100 KB raw / 25 KB gzip, or the manifest's) is a warning, never a failure: the SVG is still written and the result is still ok. The publish folder is the manifest's publish.dir (relative to the document), or --dir; with neither it refuses. Nothing is written when any source has a problem. Returns { ok, publishDir, outputs: [{ file, scene, kind (svg or png), raw, gzip, over, report, warnings }], previewOnly: [{ scene, raw, gzip, over, report, warnings }], problems, warnings (each "<file>: <warning>"), ms, unsaved }; a PNG has no gzip, over or report.

read-only · writes files directly · not an MCP tool

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir` | string |  | the folder to write the SVGs to (else the manifest's publish.dir) |

```sh
pixellab art build
pixellab art build --dir ~/Desktop/art
```

#### art.preview

Render the review PNG of an object (standing on a tile) or a scene, on the card color; `palette` for the swatch sheet.

```
pixellab art preview <name> [--scale <n>] [--kind <object|scene>] [--out <file.png>]
```

The picture an agent or a person checks art by: an object on one 32×16 tile outline, a scene at its viewBox (first variant, frame 0), both on the document's card color (manifest preview.card). Refuses (code invalid) when the doc or what it uses has problems. Returns { name, kind, scale, width, height, png } with the PNG as base64; --out writes it.

read-only · MCP tool `art_preview`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | an object or scene (or objects/<name>, scenes/<name>), or palette |
| `--scale` | integer | default `1` | whole-pixel zoom of the PNG (1 to 16) |
| `--kind` | `object` \| `scene` |  | which kind name is, when both exist |

```sh
pixellab art preview pine --scale 4 --out /tmp/pine@4x.png
pixellab art preview palette --out /tmp/palette.png
```

#### art.sizes

Bytes each object and each color adds to a compiled scene, against the document's git HEAD.

```
pixellab art sizes <name>
```

The bytes a compiled scene loses, raw and gzip, when an object's items are left out or a color's paths are dropped (costs overlap a little), now and as committed at HEAD of the repository the document is in. Returns { scene, output, now: { raw, gzip }, head: { raw, gzip } | { reason }, objects: [{ object, placed, raw, gzip, headRaw, headGzip }], colors: [{ color, raw, gzip, headRaw, headGzip }], states?: { raw, gzip, headRaw?, headGzip? }, warnings }. A scene with sprites that have states also gets states, a line of its own: the bytes of the rules in its style that play them (the objects' costs include them), as the style alone.

read-only · MCP tool `art_sizes`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | a scene (or scenes/<name>) |

```sh
pixellab art sizes hero-island
```

### chat

#### chat.ask

Ask the owner a question with two to four answers, shown as buttons in Pixel Lab's Agent chat.

```
pixellab chat ask <question> --options <text,…>
```

Use it when the owner should choose (every use of an object or only these, one way or another). It returns at once: the question shows in the chat with a button per answer, and the owner's choice arrives as their next message, so end your turn after asking. With no Pixel Lab chat on this connection (a terminal), it says so: ask in your own conversation.

read-only · MCP tool `chat_ask`

| `question` (positional) | string | required | the question, in one or two sentences |


#### chat.context

Build the selection block an Agent chat message carries: what's selected, as the saved document has it.

```
pixellab chat context [name] [--object <text>] [--layers <text,…>] [--items <text,…>] [--pinned <text,…>]
```

Pixel Lab sends this block with each chat message. Layers and items are named as the app has them (its working copy, which may have unsaved edits); the block names them by their paths in the saved file. An item placed, moved or changed since the last save, or a layer made or changed since, isn't in the saved file: it's left out and listed in unsaved. With --object, the block names a whole object instead.

read-only · MCP tool `chat_context`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string |  | scene name (or scenes/<name>) |
| `--object` | string |  | an object: the block names the whole object (object mode) instead of a scene |
| `--layers` | list of string |  | selected layer ids, comma-separated on the command line |
| `--items` | list of string |  | selected item paths (12, 5.2), comma-separated on the command line |
| `--pinned` | list of string |  | which of those are pinned to the chat: layer:<id> or a path |

```sh
pixellab chat context harbor --items 45.0,46.0 --layers boats
```

### check

#### check

Validate the sources with the engine, all of them or one doc.

```
pixellab check [name] [--kind <object|scene>] [--library <text>]
```

Problems are the engine's "<file>: <where>: <rule>" lines. With a name, only the problems in that doc and the files it uses (palette.json, the objects it places or extends) are listed. On the command line, the exit code is 1 when there are problems. Warnings don't fail the check, and each has a code. off_grid: a scene's key-to-key moves (the loop back to the first key included) whose steps aren't 1 px straight, 1:1 or 2:1, so the item jumps instead of walking the grid; scene.motion.path makes on-grid keys. out_of_order: a scene whose file lists its items out of depth order (it still publishes in depth order; scene.sort writes the file in order), with how many items would move. copies: a moving item that takes several places among the others as it moves is drawn once for each place in the SVG, which adds to its size; the warning says how many. cropped: a scene with a fixed viewBox paints pixels outside it, which the published SVG cuts off; the warning says how many (scene.frame --fit fits it to its content). empty: a scene with nothing in it and no viewBox, which publishes one tile around the origin. states_and_loops: a sprite with states that also has layer ambient loops or actions, which never play since the states decide what plays (object.states.make turns them into states). scene_owns_state: an item whose motion track keys a state sits in a group with data-state or data-play: the scene plays it, so the page's attribute can't switch it. With library, it checks an object library instead (no document needed): its objects against the colors it recorded at export, extends resolving inside it, and categories.

read-only · MCP tool `check`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string |  | an object or scene (or objects/<name>, scenes/<name>); every source when left out |
| `--kind` | `object` \| `scene` |  | which kind name is, when both exist |
| `--library` | string |  | check this .pixellib instead of the document: its objects against the colors it recorded, extends within it, categories |

```sh
pixellab check
pixellab check hero-island
pixellab check objects/pine --json
pixellab check --library ~/Art/explainer.pixellib
```

### doc

#### doc.adopt

Merge a client's unsaved copy of a doc into this one, as one step.

```
pixellab doc adopt <doc> [--base <text>] --source <text>
```

For an MCP server that edited a doc it couldn't save before Pixel Lab opened the document: base is the text it started from (null for a new doc), source its own. One undo step by that client; refuses with merge_conflict when both changed the same lines.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · not an MCP tool

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |
| `--base` | any |  | the text the copy started from |
| `--source` | string | required | the copy's text |

#### doc.close

Close an open doc (refused with unsaved changes unless --force).

```
pixellab doc close <doc> [--force]
```

read-only · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_close`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |
| `--force` | boolean | default `false` | drop unsaved changes |

#### doc.flush

Save every open doc with changes now (or one), as autosave would soon.

```
pixellab doc flush [doc]
```

Edits save themselves about a second after the last one; this saves now. A doc with problems isn't written (saveState problems), and one whose file changed on disk is merged first (saveState conflict when that clashes). Returns { saved, docs: [{ doc, saveState, problems }] }.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_flush`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string |  | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.merge

Merge the changes to a doc's file on disk into its working copy, keeping the unsaved edits.

```
pixellab doc merge <doc>
```

A three-way line merge: the file as the doc was opened or last saved, the file now, and the working copy. One undo step; the doc stays dirty with its own edits. A doc with no unsaved edits just reloads. When both sides changed the same lines it refuses with code merge_conflict (details: [{ base: [from, to], ours: [lines], theirs: [lines] }]) and changes nothing. The merged scene is put in depth order, in the same step (a line merge cannot judge overlaps): sorted says how many items moved. Returns { doc, merged, changed, summary, dirty, canUndo, canRedo, sorted? }.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_merge`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.open

Open a scene or object as a working copy, with undo and redo.

```
pixellab doc open <doc>
```

Edits to an open doc save themselves (the app's server: about a second after the last one; MCP and the CLI: after each command). Editing a doc that isn't open opens it, so this is only needed to start from a clean status.

read-only · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_open`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.redo

Redo the last undone edit to an open doc.

```
pixellab doc redo <doc>
```

A scene edit and its depth sort are one step, so undoing it can give items other paths. When it does, the result has reordered: every path that changed, old → new (an item whose placement the step changed pairs with itself), for a caller holding paths.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_redo`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.reload

Load an open doc from disk again, only if no unsaved work is lost.

```
pixellab doc reload <doc>
```

Reloads when the working copy has no edits its file lacks: it is clean, or it matches the file. Refuses with code dirty (details: the edits that would be lost) when there are unsaved edits. Returns { doc, reloaded, changed, summary, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }; reloaded is false when the doc already matched the file. A scene whose file is not in depth order (a hand edit) is sorted as a step of its own: the result has sorted (how many items moved), the doc is then unsaved, and one undo gives back exactly the file. doc.revert is the one that drops edits.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_reload`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.revert

Load an open doc from disk again, dropping its changes (as one undo step).

```
pixellab doc revert <doc>
```

A doc that was never saved (made by scene.new or object.new) is discarded. To reload without dropping anything, use doc.reload.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_revert`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` (positional) | string | required | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

#### doc.save

Save an open doc now and close its version: validate, serialize with the engine and write its source.

```
pixellab doc save <doc> [--force]
```

Edits save themselves, so this is the Mac's Save: it writes now and starts a new version for the next edit. Refuses a doc with validation problems (code invalid, details: the problems) and a file that changed on disk since the doc was opened (code conflict), unless --force. Returns { doc, file, wrote, hash, diff, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }.

edits docs · session only (`serve`) · MCP tool `doc_save`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `--force` | boolean | default `false` | save despite problems or a conflict |

#### doc.status

Whether open docs have unsaved changes, and can undo or redo.

```
pixellab doc status [doc]
```

With a doc: { doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo, undoLabel, redoLabel, author, saveState, problems, file, exists, stale, undo: [edits], redo: [edits], edits }. saveState: saved, pending (a save is coming), problems (it can't be saved until they're fixed) or conflict (its file changed on disk and clashes). undoLabel and redoLabel name the step and, for anyone but the owner, whose it is. stale: the file changed on disk since the doc was opened or last matched it. edits: the edits since the doc last matched its file. Without a doc: { docs: [{ doc, dirty, canUndo, canRedo }] }.

| param | type | | description |

| `doc` (positional) | string |  | the doc: scene:<name>, object:<name>, or a name (scenes/<name>, objects/<name>) |

Undo the last edit to an open doc.

A scene edit and its depth sort are one step, so undoing it can give items other paths. When it does, the result has reordered: every path that changed, old → new (an item whose placement the step changed pairs with itself), for a caller holding paths.

Save a copy of the open document at another path (Save As).

Copies the whole .pixellab folder (manifest, palette, objects, scenes) to --to. Refuses an existing path. The copy keeps its publish.dir, so a relative one now points next to the copy. A legacy source/ folder has no manifest: the copy gets one with the site's budgets, publish folder (..) and colors, so it publishes as the site did.

#### document.info

Show the document in use: where it came from, its publish folder and what it holds.

```
pixellab document info
```

root is the .pixellab folder (or a legacy source/ folder in a site checkout, kind legacy-site); from says how it was named (--document, --site, PIXELLAB_DOC, PIXELLAB_SITE, the config file or the default); publishDir is where art build writes (null when the manifest names none); then the git branch, and how many scenes, objects and colors it has, with the count of validation problems.

read-only · MCP tool `document_info`

#### document.migrate

Migrate a document from format 1 (.mjs sources) to format 2 (JSON sources), in place or as a copy.

```
pixellab document migrate [--to <text>]
```

Reads every .mjs source as data (comments become notes; anything that isn't plain data is refused with its file, line and column), checks that every scene builds the same SVG from the JSON sources, then writes palette.json, objects/*.json, scenes/*.json and a manifest with "format": 2. In place it removes the .mjs files (a site's legacy source/ folder becomes src/assets/pixel-art/<name>.pixellab); with --to it writes a copy and leaves the document as it is. Refuses while the document has unsaved edits open in Pixel Lab.

edits docs · writes files directly · not an MCP tool

```sh
pixellab document migrate --to /tmp/copy.pixellab
```

### library

#### library.category

Set or clear the category of objects in a .pixellib, in place.

```
pixellab library category <library> <names…> [--category <text>] [--to <text>] [--clear]
```

Writes the library's object files in place, canonical, while holding a lock on the folder. A library has no undo and no history: it is a file, and this is the only way to edit one (no painting, adding or removing objects). The rules for a category are object.category's.

#### library.export

Copies all of the document's objects, the objects of one category and everything below it, or a named list into a package of the same object files, with a record of the palette colors they use (never read as a palette). Every object that a chosen one extends comes too, marked base: true in the result, so the library stands on its own. pixellab library export ~/Art/everything.pixellib
```sh
pixellab library export ~/Art/trees.pixellib --category Nature/Trees
pixellab library export ~/Art/some.pixellib --objects pine,tree
```

#### library.import

Import the objects of a .pixellib into the document, by copying.

```
pixellab library import <from> [--accept-differences] [--convert <json>] [--dry-run]
```

Copies the library's objects, with their categories, into the document; nothing links it to the library afterwards, and the same library can be imported again. An imported object whose name is taken gets the first free suffix (pine-2) and every extends in the import follows; the document's own objects are never renamed or changed. One that equals the document's same-named object, apart from its category, isn't copied (fate same). A library's character that differs from the document's isn't copied: its figures extend the document's character, which counts as a difference. The plan (dryRun returns it): objects with their fate (new, renamed, same, character), renames, differing colors, the character swap, and missing colors with each one's tier and the document's nearest color of that tier. Refusals, each carrying the plan in its details: differs (colors that differ from the library's record, or the character swap) unless acceptDifferences; missing_colors unless convert names a color for every missing one; wrong_tier when a conversion crosses tiers (an outfit color converts only to an outfit color); invalid when the library or the result doesn't pass check. An agent that hits differs or missing_colors asks the owner with chat_ask before accepting or converting. The import never changes the palette, the existing objects or the scenes. It is one version in the history (Imported 12 objects from explainer.pixellib), whose number is in the result, and one undo step: history_undo takes it back.

edits docs · writes files directly · MCP tool `library_import`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` (positional) | string | required | the .pixellib folder |
| `--accept-differences` | boolean | default `false` | import although colors differ from the library's record, or its character differs |
| `--convert` | object |  | for each color the document lacks, the document's color of the same tier to use instead: {"wood-5": "wood-3"} |
| `--dry-run` | boolean | default `false` | return the plan and change nothing |

```sh
pixellab library import ~/Art/explainer.pixellib --dry-run
pixellab library import ~/Art/explainer.pixellib --accept-differences --convert '{"wood-5":"wood-3"}'
```

#### object.category

Set or clear the category of one or more objects.

```
pixellab object category <names…> [--category <text>] [--to <text>] [--clear]
```

A category is a path of names, outermost first (Nature › Trees), that groups an object under a tab and heading in the Library. A name is 1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, &, ' or -, with no space at either end or doubled, and All and Others can't be the outermost (they are the Library's own tabs). Names compare without regard to case. A category never changes how an object renders or what Publish writes. Give --to on the command line, or category (a list, or null to clear) in JSON. Each object is its own edit and undo step; the command checks every object and the path first.

#### object.footprint

Set how many tiles a sprite covers (--to w,d), or clear it (--clear).

```
pixellab object footprint <name> [--to <n,…>] [--clear]
```

A sprite sorts against its neighbours in depth order by the ground it covers: a footprint of [wide, deep] tiles from the tile it's placed on, so a house, a locomotive or the crane mast go in front of and behind things by the tiles under them. The default is 1,1. A block's size is its footprint, so blocks refuse this. An object that extends another has the other's footprint unless it sets its own. The scenes that use it are put in order again at their next edit; check warns until then (scene.sort does it now).

#### object.map.set

Replace a whole map of a sprite's layer (or frame of a loop) from rows, in one undo step.

```
pixellab object map set <name> <rows…> [--keys <json>] [--layer <n>] [--frame <n>] [--resize]
```

Rows are strings of one character per pixel, top to bottom, '.' transparent. With --keys (a legend, { char: color }), each legend character becomes the object's key for that color, made if it has none, so a generated map can use any characters; without, the characters are the object's own keys. Checks the palette, outfit colors (only for objects that extend character), the 12-color cap and the 64×64 size cap. A size other than the object's is refused unless --resize, which pads or crops every map first (as object.resize). On an object that extends another, a still layer's rows become row overrides. Blocks are refused: paint their surface and sides.

#### object.render

Render one object to a transparent PNG.

```
pixellab object render <name> [--scale <n>] [--frame <n>] [--time <n>] [--state <text>] [--play <text>] [--layers <n,…>] [--out <file.png>]
```

The anchor is at (0, 0). A sprite's viewBox is its whole map, so at scale 1 PNG pixel (x, y) is map column x, row y; a block's is the box around its pixels. Returns the same shape as scene.render, with one item. A sprite with states shows the one it starts in --time ms after time 0, or --state's from its first frame, and the item says its state and frame. --time also places the layers' ambient loops, and --play <action>@<ms> (with --time) places the layers that have that action where it has them <ms> into it; with --time the viewBox grows to hold the moved layers (the map's box, plus what moved outside it), and viewBox says where. On the command line, --out <file.png> writes the PNG.

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | object name (or objects/<name>) |
| `--scale` | integer | default `1` | whole-pixel zoom of the PNG (1 to 16) |
| `--frame` | integer | default `0` | the frame every loop shows (loops shorter than this show nothing) (at least 0) |

#### object.state.add

Add a state to a sprite: frames played at one frame length, that loops or plays once.

```
pixellab object state add <name> <state> [--frames <n,…>] [--ms <n>] [--once] [--then <text>] [--after <text>]
```

A state is the sprite's frames played at one frame length; it loops, or plays once and then holds its last frame or hands over to another state (--once --then). Without --frames it plays every frame, and without --ms it uses the frame length the sprite's frame loop plays at today (150 ms for ff, 200 ms for wf, 500 ms for hf, 200 ms for any other loop and for a still sprite), so the first state looks and plays as the sprite did. The first state is the start: every placement plays it unless an item says otherwise. A sprite has at most 32 states, and a block or a sprite that extends another has none of its own. The names clear and start are the scene commands' words and can't be state names, and neither can names that start as the compiler's own do (mv-, am-, a or s and a number, like s2).

edits docs · MCP tool `object_state_add`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | object name (or objects/<name>) |
| `state` (positional) | string | required | the new state's name: lowercase words joined by hyphens |
| `--frames` | list of integer |  | the frames it plays, in order: frame numbers of the sprite, repeats allowed (on the command line 0,1,2) |
| `--ms` | integer |  | how long each frame shows, in ms (20 to 10000) |
| `--once` | boolean | default `false` | play once, then hold the last frame (or hand over, with --then) |
| `--then` | string |  | with --once: the state that follows |
| `--after` | string |  | the state it goes after in the list (default: last) |

```sh
pixellab object state add lamp idle
pixellab object state add lamp flicker --frames 0,1,0,1 --ms 80 --once --then idle
```

#### object.state.run

What a state plays: the states it leads through, where it settles, and when its frame or move changes.

```
pixellab object state run <name> <state> [--horizon <n>]
```

The run is what an item shows after it enters the state, and it is the same every time: segments are the states that then leads through (each from and to, in ms after entering), settle says where it ends up (a loop from some ms with its period, or a hold of one frame), and changes lists every time the frame or the whole sprite's move (x,y pixels) changes, from 0 up to horizon. The app, the renders and the published SVG all play this one run.

#### object.states.make

Turn a sprite's layer ambient loop and actions into states.

```
pixellab object states make <name>
```

For moving a sprite over to states (the site's character, for one). The ambient loop becomes the start state, idle: it loops, the layer's move is the sprite's move and its length the loop's duration. Each action becomes a state of the same name that plays once with the action's move and then hands over to idle. The sprite's frames carry over, and the layer's ambient and actions are taken off. It refuses, and says why, when it couldn't keep the art the same: an ambient loop that starts part-way in (an offset), moves on more than one layer, a move on a layer while another has pixels, or a duration that isn't a whole number of the frame loop's cycles. A scene item's own ambient and actions stay as they are.

#### palette.import

Add the colors of a .pixelpal file the document doesn't have.

```
pixellab palette import <from> [--keep <text,…>] [--use-theirs <text,…>] [--only <text,…>] [--dry-run]
```

Adds each color the document doesn't have, by name, to its tier at the end of it, with the file's note for it. It never removes a color; a color with the same name and value is left alone. A name the document has with another value is listed as differing, and the import refuses (palette_differs) until each is in keep or useTheirs; a name that is in the other tier in the file is listed in otherTier and stays as the document has it. When adding would pass a tier's cap (32 world colors, 16 outfit colors) nothing is added: it refuses (palette_full) saying how many colors are over, and only narrows the import to a chosen list. dryRun returns the plan. One edit, one undo step and one version (Imported 4 colors from coast.pixelpal). An agent that hits palette_differs asks the owner with chat_ask before choosing.

### scene

#### scene.action

Add, change or delete a scene item's action: a one-shot move the page plays by name.

```
pixellab scene action <name> <item> <action> [--duration <n>] [--keys <json,…>] [--delete]
```

An action plays when the page names it in data-play (the site contract's actions), replaces the item's ambient loop while it plays, holds its last key until --duration ms, then the item is back at rest. --keys is as for scene ambient. Giving a name the item has changes it; --delete removes it. An item has at most 16 actions, and a name is one move in a scene. scene render --play <action>@<ms> shows a frame of it.

edits docs · MCP tool `scene_action`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | scene name (or scenes/<name>) |
| `item` (positional) | string | required | the item: its path from scene items (12, 5.2) or its id |
| `action` (positional) | string | required | the action's name: lowercase words joined by hyphens, like hop |
| `--duration` | integer |  | the action's length in ms, up to 600000 (at least 1) |
| `--keys` | list of object |  | the keys, a JSON list of { "t": ms, "move": [x, y] }: the first at t 0, each after the one before and below the duration, moves in whole pixels from where the art is drawn. On the command line, the list as one JSON string. |
| `--delete` | boolean | default `false` | delete the action instead |

```sh
pixellab scene action meadow frog hop --duration 480 --keys '[{"t":0,"move":[0,0]},{"t":120,"move":[0,-4]}]'
pixellab scene action meadow frog hop --delete
```

#### scene.ambient

Set or clear a scene item's ambient loop: a move that repeats on its own.

```
pixellab scene ambient <name> <item> [--duration <n>] [--offset <n>] [--keys <json,…>] [--clear]
```

The loop lasts --duration ms and starts --offset ms in. --keys is a JSON list of { "t", "move" }: the first at t 0, each later one after the one before and below the duration; the item is moved by [x, y] whole pixels from where the scene places it, stepping a pixel at a time between keys, and after the last key it steps back to the first over the rest of the duration. It plays in the SVG on its own, and scene render --time places it. Setting replaces the loop the item has. --clear removes it. An item with scene motion can't also have an ambient loop. An edit that would leave the scene with a problem is refused, and nothing changes.

| `--clear` | boolean | default `false` | remove the ambient loop instead |


#### scene.drop

Drop an item onto whatever it stands over: down to the top of the block under it, or the ground.

```

```

As the lab's Drop key: the item's level becomes the one where it rests on the highest block under its column and row (a block of height h rests with its bottom on it), or level 0, the ground, when nothing is under it. It never moves up; an item already resting stays. One undo step. The item's group's data-x/data-y follow, as scene.move keeps them (--no-keep-group leaves them), and the scene is put in depth order.

#### scene.frame

Show a scene's published size, fix it (--box), fit it to its content (--fit) or set its margin.

```
pixellab scene frame <name> [--box <n,…>] [--fit] [--margin <n>]
```

A scene with a viewBox publishes at exactly that box (fixed). One without publishes at the smallest whole-pixel box that holds everything it paints, over its whole loop (scene motion, ambient loops and actions included), plus its margin (fit). --box x,y,w,h fixes the size; --fit removes the viewBox so the scene fits its content again; --margin n sets the pixels left around a fit scene's art (a fixed box ignores it). With none of them it reports the frame: { frame: "fixed" | "fit", viewBox, size: [w, h], margin }. One undo step, saved like every edit.

#### scene.items

List a scene's items in depth order (back to front), with stable paths.

```
pixellab scene items <name>
```

Paths index into the scene's items: "3" is the fourth top-level item, "5.2" the third item inside the group at "5". The list is in depth order (every edit keeps it so; scene.sort fixes a file that isn't): back to front, by where each item stands. Each item has its object, at ({ tile: [col, row, level] } or { px: [x, y], level? }), level (a pixel item's, 0 unless it says), depth (front or back, when it has the override), class, id, layer, enclosing group and placement point in scene pixels. A group in groups has its path, attrs, item count and depth. layers lists the scene's layers ({ id, name, parent, items }: items counts what is in it and in the layers inside it), in the order the Layers panel shows them.

#### scene.key.set

Set a key of an item's track: its move, show, pose and state at a time (made if there's no key there).


--move x,y is pixels from where the scene places the item; --show false hides it from that key on; --pose <object> draws another object from that key on; --state <name> puts it in that state of the object it shows (a state is entered from its first frame and plays by itself, the same every time; --state clear takes it off the key). #### scene.layer.move

Move layers (every item in them, and in the layers inside them) and items by tiles, together.

```
pixellab scene layer move <name> [layer] [--layers <text,…>] [--items <text,…>] --by <n,…> [--keep-group]
```

As dragging a selection on the stage: every item moves by --by col,row[,level] tiles (a pixel-placed item by the same screen offset), each once, in one undo step; rapid repeats coalesce. Placements move at rest: an animated item's keys are offsets from its placement, so its motion moves with it. Each item's group keeps its data-x/data-y and data-col/data-row in step, as scene.move does (--no-keep-group leaves them). Each item then stands at a new depth, so the scene is put in depth order: paths lists the moved items' paths after that, and reordered says which other paths moved. Layers themselves never change what is published.

#### scene.layer.new

Make a layer (a named, nestable part of a scene) and move items and layers into it.

```
pixellab scene layer new <name> [--layer-name <text>] [--id <text>] [--items <text,…>] [--layers <text,…>] [--parent <text>]
```

A layer names part of a scene (the Mine, the Railway, the Train inside it) so it can be selected, moved and placed into as one. It never changes paint order or what is published: items keep their place in the scene, and their { group } wrappers stay as they are. Without --layer-name it is "Group n". Its parent is --parent ('' for the top level), else the deepest layer that holds every member, else the top level. A member already inside another member stays where it is. Its id is made from the name unless --id gives one. Returns the layer, how many items joined it and which layers.

#### scene.motion.path

Key an item along a polyline on the grid, at a steady speed or between two times.

```
pixellab scene motion path <name> <item> <points…> [--start <n>] [--speed <n>] [--end <n>]
```

--points are moves (pixels from where the scene places the item), the first at --start. Each segment is split into runs that step 1 px straight, 1:1 or 2:1, each ending in a key; times follow the distance at --speed px per second, or spread from --start to --end. Keys inside the path lose their move (and go, if that leaves nothing); a key there with show or pose keeps its place on the path. Makes the track if the item (with an id) has none. Returns the keys written and the track's remaining off-grid warnings (such as the step from the path's end to the next key).

edits docs · MCP tool `scene_motion_path`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | scene name (or scenes/<name>) |
| `item` (positional) | string | required | the item: its path from scene items (12, 5.2) or its id; an item needs an id to have a track (scene.set --id) |
| `points` (positional) | list of [integer, …] | required | x,y moves along the path; on the command line x,y pairs separated by spaces |
| `--start` | integer | default `0` | when the path starts, ms into the loop (at least 0) |
| `--speed` | number |  | pixels per second along the path |
| `--end` | integer |  | when the path ends, ms into the loop (instead of --speed) (at least 0) |

```sh
pixellab scene motion path hero-island truck-a 0,0 16,-3 48,-3 --start 2000 --speed 20
```

#### scene.move

Move an item by tiles and levels (--by) or by pixels (--nudge).

```
pixellab scene move <name> <item> [--keep-group] [--by <n,…>] [--nudge <n,…>] [--time <n>]
```

As the lab's arrow keys: --by col,row[,level] moves an item on a tile by whole tiles (a pixel-placed item moves by the same screen offset, and its level by the same levels, so it stands over the same tile a level higher); --nudge x,y moves it by pixels, and an item on a tile is then placed by pixel at the level it stood on. With --time past 0, an animated item (one with an id and a motion track) moves at that time instead: the key there, made if needed, takes the move. Rapid repeats coalesce into one undo step. A move at rest keeps the item's group in step: data-x/data-y that were its placement point or foot, and data-col/data-row that were its tile, follow it (--no-keep-group leaves them); the result has the group when they did. The scene is then put in depth order: the result has the item's path after that, and reordered says which other paths moved.

edits docs · MCP tool `scene_move`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | scene name (or scenes/<name>) |
| `item` (positional) | string | required | the item: its path from scene items (12, 5.2) or its id |
| `--keep-group` | boolean | default `true` | keep the item's group in step: data-x/data-y that were its placement point or foot, and data-col/data-row that were its tile, follow it |
| `--by` | list of integer |  | tiles to move: col,row[,level] |
| `--nudge` | list of integer |  | pixels to move: x,y |
| `--time` | integer | default `0` | ms into the scene's motion; past 0 an animated item's key moves (at least 0) |

```sh
pixellab scene move hero-island 0.0 --by 1,0
pixellab scene move hero-island jib --nudge 0,-1 --dry-run
```

#### scene.place

Place an object on a tile (or at a pixel point) in a scene.

```
pixellab scene place <name> <object> [--at <n,…>] [--px <n,…>] [--level <n>] [--on-top] [--class <text>] [--id <text>] [--group <text>] [--new-group <json>] [--foot] [--layer <text>]
```

Like the lab's Place tool, but the item goes where it stands: it is added to its list and the scene's items are put in depth order, so it draws behind what is in front of it and over what is behind (scene.items shows the order). With neither --at nor --px, it goes on the tile at the middle of the view, where the lab's cursor starts (the middle of the scene's content when it has no viewBox). With no level given (--at col,row, or no position) it stands on top of whatever block covers that tile: on the highest one there, in whole levels, or on the ground (level 0); a block of height h rests with its bottom on that top. --at col,row,level is used as given unless --on-top is set, which also works for --px. --px takes --level, how high the item stands (default 0), which is only for depth: its pixel point is where its foot is drawn. --group puts it inside an existing group (the group's path, or an item inside it); --new-group wraps it in a new group with those attributes (class and data-*, like {"class": "enter", "data-enter": "object"}), and --foot sets that group's data-x and data-y to the item's foot. --layer puts it in a scene layer (its id or name; layers are apart from groups and never change paint order). Returns the new item's path after the sort, and its group's; reordered says which other paths the sort moved.

edits docs · MCP tool `scene_place`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | scene name (or scenes/<name>) |
| `object` (positional) | string | required | the object to place |
| `--at` | list of integer |  | a tile: col,row[,level]; without a level the item goes on top of what stands there |
| `--px` | list of integer |  | a point in scene pixels: x,y |
| `--level` | integer |  | with --px: how high the item stands, for depth order (default 0) |
| `--on-top` | boolean | default `false` | put the item on top of the block on its tile, whatever level --at or --px give |
| `--class` | string |  | a class list for the item |
| `--id` | string |  | an id for the item (lowercase kebab-case, unique in the scene) |
| `--group` | string |  | an existing group to place it in: its path, or an item (path or id) inside it |
| `--new-group` | object |  | attributes of a new group around the item (class, data-*), as JSON on the command line |
| `--foot` | boolean | default `false` | with --new-group: set its data-x and data-y to the item's foot |
| `--layer` | string |  | a layer of the scene for the new item to join: its id, or its name (scene items lists them) |

```sh
pixellab scene place hero-island pine --at 14,6,1
pixellab scene place range-sprite boxes --px 40,12 --dry-run
pixellab scene place hero-island crane-jib --px 40,-12 --level 4
pixellab scene place hero-island crate --at 3,1,1 --new-group '{"class": "enter", "data-enter": "object"}' --foot
pixellab scene place hero-island pine --at 3,1,1 --layer railway
```

#### scene.render

Render a scene to a transparent PNG, with item bounds.

```
pixellab scene render <name> [--scale <n>] [--time <n>] [--theme <light|dark>] [--play <text>] [--view <n,…>] [--show <text>] [--hide <text,…>] [--focus <text>] [--out <file.png>]
```

Returns { png (base64), scale, viewBox, frame, width, height, time, items: [{ path, object, at, id, bounds: [x, y, w, h] }] }. viewBox is the box the scene publishes at (its own, or the fit to what it paints; frame says which: "fixed" or "fit"), or the --view window when one is given. Bounds are in output pixels (scale included), for hit-testing. Of each run of data-class variant groups only the first shows, or the one holding --show. --hide leaves out the items in those layers (and the layers inside them) and the items at those paths, as hiding them in Pixel Lab does (a name that is a layer wins over a path); --focus adds focusPng, the same render with only that layer's items. Ambient loops are placed at --time; --play <action>@<ms> places the elements that have that action where it has them <ms> into it. On the command line, --out <file.png> writes the PNG.

read-only · MCP tool `scene_render`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string | required | scene name (or scenes/<name>) |
| `--scale` | integer | default `1` | whole-pixel zoom of the PNG (1 to 16) |
| `--time` | integer |  | ms into the animation: frame loops and motion tracks (default 0, the rest frame) (at least 0) |
| `--theme` | `light` \| `dark` | default `"light"` | dark draws as the site's dark theme: the hero island's drop shadow (data-enter="shadow") takes the dark page color |
| `--play` | string |  | an action and the ms into it, like hop@120: the elements that have it are placed where it has them then, instead of on their ambient loop |
| `--view` | list of integer |  | a window of the scene to render instead of its whole box: x,y,w,h in scene pixels (the result's viewBox is then the window) |
| `--show` | string |  | an item path whose variant group to show, like 12.0 |
| `--hide` | list of string |  | layers (ids or names) whose items are left out, or item paths like 12.0 to leave out single items |
| `--focus` | string |  | a layer: the result adds focusPng, the render of only its items (and those of the layers inside it) |

```sh
pixellab scene render hero-island --scale 2 --out /tmp/hero.png
pixellab scene render range-sprite --time 400 --json
pixellab scene render hero-island --theme dark --out /tmp/hero-dark.png
pixellab scene render meadow --play hop@120 --out /tmp/hop.png
```

#### scene.set

Set an item's tile or pixel point, one coordinate, its level, depth override, class, id or state.

```
pixellab scene set <name> <item> [--keep-group] [--tile <n,…>] [--px <n,…>] [--col <n>] [--row <n>] [--level <n>] [--x <n>] [--y <n>] [--depth <front|back|auto>] [--class <text>] [--id <text>] [--state <text>]
```

--tile col,row,level or --px x,y place the item there (changing how it's placed if need be; a pixel point keeps the level the item stands on); --col, --row, --level (an item on a tile) and --x, --y (a pixel-placed item) set one coordinate, like the lab's Selected fields. --level also sets how high a pixel-placed item stands, which only matters for depth order. --depth is the override: front draws the item over everything else in its list, back under everything, auto takes the override off so it draws by where it stands. It also takes a group's path, as the only field (a group's attributes are scene.group.set). --class sets the class list and --id the id; an empty value removes it. --state sets the state of its object the item starts in (the object's start otherwise; --state start puts it back). An id's motion track follows it when it's renamed and goes with it when it's removed. All in one undo step, after which the scene is in depth order (the result has the item's path after that; reordered says what moved). Moving it keeps its group's data-x/data-y and data-col/data-row in step, as scene.move does (--no-keep-group leaves them).

#### scene.sort

Put a scene's items (or every scene's) in depth order, and say what moved.

```
pixellab scene sort [name] [--all]
```

Every edit to a scene already keeps its items in depth order (back to front, by where each stands); this is for a scene whose file isn't, such as one written by hand or made before depth order. A group sorts as one object and its members sort inside it. One undo step per scene. Returns { moved: [{ scene, path, to, object | group }], changedPixels, scenes: [{ scene, moved, changedPixels }] }: moved lists the items the sort took out of their place (paths before and after), and changedPixels counts the pixels that differ at time 0 between the scene drawn in its file's list order (as engines before depth order publish it) and in depth order, which is what the site sees when it adopts this engine. Give a scene or --all. For one scene, reordered maps every path the sort changed to its new path. With --dry-run on the command line nothing is written and the diff shows the new order.

edits docs · MCP tool `scene_sort`

| param | type | | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (positional) | string |  | scene name (or scenes/<name>); leave out with --all |
| `--all` | boolean | default `false` | sort every scene |

```sh
pixellab scene sort hero-island --dry-run
pixellab scene sort --all
```

#### scene.track.add

Add a motion track for an item: one key at 0, the rest frame.

```
pixellab scene track add <name> <item> [--duration <n>]
```

Makes the scene's motion (one loop of --duration ms) when it has none. An item without an id gets one, its object's name made unique in the scene (cart, cart-2), and the result says which (id). Then scene.key.set or scene.motion.path keys it.
